D: Axial DWI MRI panel demonstrates restricted diffusion in the cerebellar white matter/vermis and dorsal brainstem, consistent with MSUD.

A: Panel A is an axial brain MRI from a patient with maple syrup urine disease, showing FLAIR hyperintense signal in the bilateral globus pallidum and other characteristic locations. B: Panel B is an axial diffusion-weighted brain MRI from a patient with maple syrup urine disease, showing diffusion restriction in the bilateral globus pallidum and posterior limb of the internal capsule, classic for MSUD encephalopathy. Thalamic and genu involvement are also described but lack matching vocabulary keys.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Axial FLAIR MRI panel in a neonatal MSUD case shows subtle hyperintense signals in the optic chiasma, pons, vermis, and cerebellum, consistent with MSUD neuroimaging involvement, plus a mild subdural collection. The finding is real-patient radiology with arrows; no matched vocabulary term for FLAIR hyperintensity is available, so it is listed as a proposed finding. B: Axial diffusion-weighted MRI panel in a neonatal MSUD case shows restricted diffusion in the pons, vermis, and cerebellum, matching characteristic MSUD brainstem and cerebellar white matter involvement.

panels.figure_caption: Diffusion-weighted axial images (superior row) and ADC axial images (inferior row) obtained in a newborn with a biochemically confirmed classical form of maple syrup urine disease. He was admitted with severe encephalopathy and coma. The myelinated areas shown as symmetrical, markedly high intensity signal on a rather homogeneous brain parenchyma depict the cortico-spinal tract (a, b) and the cerebello-pontine white matter (c). Restricted diffusion of water molecules is well demonstrated by ADC images (d, e, f)
in_text_mentions: RI may provide a highly suggestive pattern of lesions with a generalised cerebral oedema and a striking increase in DWI and T2 signal intensity in all areas that are already myelinated at birth (Fig. 2). At microscopic examination the same areas represent myelin splitting and intra-myelin vacuoles. These peculiar histological changes are thought to explain the observed reduction in ADC values and its reversibility. Early diagnosis and treatment may normalise clinical and neuroradiological abnormalities, although inter-current illnesses throughout life may lead to further metabolic derangements
